questions.q: What is Smart View, in terms of what kind of software it is?
options: A standalone web application with no relationship to Microsoft Office
A Microsoft Office add-in, most commonly used in Excel
A command-line tool for database administrators
A mobile-only application
questions.explain: Smart View installs as a Microsoft Office add-in, appearing in Excel, Word, and PowerPoint with its own ribbon.

questions.q: How is Smart View different from simply exporting a one-time snapshot of data into Excel?
options: There is no real difference
Smart View cannot be refreshed once connected
Smart View keeps a live connection, so a worksheet can be refreshed to pull current balances again
Smart View only works with static CSV files
questions.explain: Unlike a static export, Smart View maintains a live connection that lets a user refresh and pull current data repeatedly.

questions.q: What is a "shared connection" in Smart View used for?
options: Sharing an Excel file with coworkers over email
Scheduling a BI Publisher report
Creating a new OTBI subject area
Pointing Smart View at the specific Oracle Fusion environment to connect to
questions.explain: A shared connection is essentially a URL configuration that tells Smart View which Fusion instance to communicate with.

questions.q: Does Smart View use its own separate login and security rules, apart from the rest of Oracle Fusion?
options: Yes, Smart View has a completely independent security system
Smart View requires no authentication at all
No — signing into Smart View uses the same Oracle Fusion credentials and the same underlying security model as other tools
Smart View security is managed only through Microsoft, not Oracle
questions.explain: Smart View relies on the same Oracle Fusion credentials and security model (duty roles, data security) covered earlier in the course.

questions.q: If a client reports "Smart View won't connect," what should be checked first, based on the troubleshooting instinct from earlier in the course?
options: Whether the issue is actually a data security or duty role problem, rather than assuming Smart View itself is broken
Immediately reinstall Microsoft Office
Whether the client has a printer configured
Whether BI Publisher is installed
questions.explain: Because Smart View shares the application's security model, a connection failure is often rooted in data security or duty role access rather than a Smart View-specific defect.
